public_rationale: He says that, based on Anthropic's March affidavit, the company appears to have spent $3 on compute for each $1 of revenue. The affidavit says Anthropic spent over $10 billion on training and inference and earned more than $5 billion in revenue. That is about $2 per $1. Anthropic's S-1 lists 2023 to 2025 revenue totaling $5.01 billion and compute and infrastructure expense totaling $10.28 billion. Those totals match the affidavit's figures and give about $2.05 per $1. His word 'appears' fairly marks this as an inference. But the document he relies on points to about 2 to 1, not 3 to 1. His broader point stands: compute alone cost about twice the revenue before other costs.
limitations: The affidavit gives only floors, so on its own it cannot fix an exact ratio. The S-1 figures settle the ratio for the matching period.
The S-1 line 'compute and infrastructure' may include some items beyond training and inference. That would make the true training-plus-inference ratio lower, not higher.
The S-1 summary table does not say whether these figures are audited.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Per its March 2026 affidavit, Anthropic appears to have spent $3 on compute for every $1 of revenue, before other costs.

statement.excerpt: Anthropic — based on its own affidavit from March — appears to have spent $3 to make $1 of revenue on a compute basis, and that’s before you include any and all other costs like staff or electricity or the vocal coach that Dario Amodei uses to add that bass to his voice.

our_interpretation: The claim is an inference drawn from a named document: CFO Krishna Rao's March 2026 declaration. The test is whether that document's compute and revenue figures, read as an informed reader would, point to roughly $3 of compute spending per $1 of revenue.

'Appears' marks the figure as an inference rather than a disclosed number. It is not treated as a strict threshold. But the inference still has to match the figures he cites. If the document's own numbers point clearly to a different ratio, the inference does not hold.
Anthropic's later S-1 annual figures, which add up to the affidavit's totals, are used to check what the true cumulative ratio was for the same period.
'Compute basis' is read as training plus inference spending (the affidavit's category), or the S-1 line 'compute and infrastructure'.
criteria.support_condition: The affidavit's figures, or audited figures for the same cumulative period, show roughly $3 (say $2.5 or more) of compute spending per $1 of revenue.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The affidavit's figures and the company's audited cumulative figures for the same period point to a clearly different ratio, such as about $2 per $1.
